As a massive fan of the original trilogy, this game is a shell of the series' former self. The dialogue is cringey, the companions are very one dimensional (excluding a couple of people), and while the game has a nice new shiny coat of paint, it lacks ALL the soul of the original games.

I wish I could recommend it, but finishing it made me really sad.
It's not a game for long time Dragon Age fans, it's not even a Dragon Age game. It's barely an RPG, you play a predetermined character. Some companions are great, the others are OK, but it feels like 50 or so hours of content is just missing? Where is the rest of the game?
Previous games I replayed multiple times, Inquisiton I finished at least 5 times, and Veilguard has 0 replayability for me.
I will complete the rest of the achievements, and then uninstall it.

I'm honestly just depressed.

I love rpgs and have played most of the main titles including all the prior dragon age. This one....really doesn't do it. I'm normally a completionist, but this is probably one of the only games i've gotten where i've just uninstalled after maybe sinking 30-40 hrs in.

I really tried to like it and I thought maybe I just need to get far enough in to get hooked, but nope. The way the lore is presented is uninspired, the combat gets dull and repetitive very quickly, the romance and dialogue is forced, the whole gender identity thing is shoved down your throat, and i don't feel anything toward the companions. The only positive thing i have to say is that the graphics and settings are...okay. inquisition still did it so much better. and the dragons? Theyre all exactly the same attack patterns. just the same thing over and over. Did not care what reagents/minerals/items i was collecting, and the weapon builds/upgrades were underwhelming.

Really just a very, very average title. 4/10. It runs smooth, it's set in a well established world, and the controls work, but otherwise meh.

Dragon Age™: The Veilguard looks like a strong and confident new step for the series. The visuals are impressive, the world feels more alive and cinematic, and the characters already show a lot of personality. Combat also appears faster and more modern while still keeping the fantasy style that makes Dragon Age unique.

BioWare deserves real credit for how it handled diversity in Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Instead of treating representation as something superficial, the game integrates it naturally into the world, the characters, and the story. The cast feels genuinely varied in culture, identity, and personality, and it never feels forced or artificial. What stands out most is that diversity actually strengthens the narrative: different perspectives make the companions more believable and the world more immersive.

Being a huge fan of the previous Dragon Age games, I was eagerly awaiting the latest installment. To say I was disappointed is an understatement. It may have beautiful graphics but that's where the wonder stops. I found creating a character more fun and engaging than playing the game itself. The script is probably one of the worst I've ever seen in any game I've played over the last 5 years. The characters are all caricatures of archetypes with no real personality or depth. The relationships between characters are shallow. There is no conflict or friction leading to overly sanitised and boring interactions with no stakes. The lore which was painstakingly created and built over multiple games was glossed over and clumsily retconned. Overall it feels as though the people who created this game had no love for the series, its fans, or gamers in general. What a pity.

I tried. I tried damn hard to like it, even liked it at first like ten-ish hours. I waited for this damn game for a long time along with other long time DA fans and so I was ready to like it. It's pretty, yes. Is it polished from technical standpoint? Well, sure. It's even sometimes fun and at first feels promising. And it all is downhill from there. It's has nothing to do with artificial hate because most valid criticism comes from people that love franchise dearly. Everything others point out regarding this game is true. It's boring. It's bland. It's woefully childish in tone. It was hard to listen to dialogues, it was friggin hard to like companions, and first time playing Dragon Age game I went with romancing character and just dropped it because it was totally dissatisfying. Over the top villains and goody-two-shoes main character you mandatory have to play, companion quests that feel sloppily written and ruined lore we all loved - it just made my experience unbelievably frustrating.
I felt better when I dropped and uninstalled it. Like it was right thing to do. Not once I felt this way with previous DA games. And I mourn the game it could maybe be if not for a corporate greed.
Is it worth playing at all? As stand alone it wouldn't be as bad (though still maybe not good). But as Dragon Age game it fails spectacularly.

I 100%'d it so you don't have to, you're welcome.

Avoid it like the plague if you have any respect at all for the older games, this is no da game. I've beaten all the previous games 5+ times on nightmare. Til now I have NEVER beaten a da game and been thankful that it was over, but that was certainly the case with this abomination. RIP bioware, mass effect is cooked if its going to look anything like this

I played Origins when it came out back in the day, have played all of the DA games and read all of the books and can say without reservation that this game is great. The characters are all interesting and while the game starts with a bit of a 'go team' cheery attitude it improves later, becoming more serious as the stakes get higher. The set pieces and the graphics in general are absolutely gorgeous and some of the darker ones like the Hossberg Wetlands and the Deep Roads are fantastic. The story builds on a lot of points from earlier games and didn't leave me disappointed. 

The combat is fast and fun, and while a deviation from previous games, still has some depth to it in terms of combos and damage types, plus a lot of weapons and armour with their own unique abilities. Skills can be respecced at any time, so you're free to try out different builds (within your chosen class) at any time. Lots of fun.

I see a lot of people trashing this for not being like the old games, and well, things change. If you can move on from Origins and give this a chance it really is a great DA experience.

If youre into the games that push pronouns, by all means, buy it. If youre into non straight relationships buy it. If youre into dying a million times by the same boss because you have to fight it multiple times, buy it.

If youre not into that, dont buy it. I wish I wouldve saved my money, Dragon Age was once a decent title.

As a Dragon Age fan i was hoping with all my heart that this game would be good. It's not terrible, but there's really not much to it. Unfortunately, the game had a troubled development and it shows.

From the story, the characters, the combat system and the level design, the game lacks depth. I wouldn't say it's the bare minimum for a AAA game, but it's not far from it and it pains me to say that.

When you compare the characters with the ones from previous entries, as well as the dialogue choices and the impact our decisions had on the story in those games, there really is no comparison.

It's a shame because after so many years and so much anticipation from both myself and DA fans, i expected something much more ambitious.

5/10 and i'm being a bit generous.

Glad i didn't listen to all the opinions around this game and just tried it. Absolutely amazing !!!

linear, repetitive, sanitized, small.

previous dragon age games suffered from overcorrection, but they were always a cohesive unit together in core matters, especially in lore and story. this is pretending to be something it's not, and hurting for it on both accords.

nothing from previous games matter— fine. that should at least mean the rpg elements of this game should be stronger. it's the opposite. the player character is neither fleshed out enough to love as a character nor allow role play as anything but a wooden puppet serving their companions instead of experiencing their own journey.

despite access to a large portion of the world, it feels so incredibely small. the world feels so hollow and uninhabited beyond npcs required to interact with. the dialogues are clumsy, characters constantly repeat themselves and lack cohesion. the combat, while fun, is repetitive. it very quickly becomes just going through the motions.

the companions are the best part of it. i really mean it, and it's sad that the story failed them. their quests vary in quality and relevance. the inclusivity also means a whole lot to me. i really wish it could shine in better ways.

it's not the worst game in the world. but in contemplation, it's simply not worth the money.
Once you accept it's different from the other dragon age games, you can appreciate the grand story and the incredibly epic boss fights

I love the character creator, spent a lot of my time there. The music is passible, it could also have more of a presence in open play but it isn't that big of a deal. (also, I believe in Neve supremacy)

Really wish I didn't listen to everyone when this first came out. I've been playing this thing like it allowed me to breathe. I like the combat more than inquisition, but there's an item in the game that basically lets you play like Inquisition by changing the abilities into a true cooldown instead of a resource pool. I enjoy all the characters, they have some great interactions, and no body feels bad to take along so no one gets left behind level wise like I've done in previous titles. I even got to the "dreaded" Taash scene and while out of context it comes across as cringe, with the backstory you're given up to that point it comes across just fine. Especially if you take the dialogue options that position you as a supportive family member. I'm already pumped for a second playthru and I'm 70 hours in.

While the dialogue can be a bit clunky at times and many people are upset in regards to lore in previous games I loved the game. It was a lot of fun and the fighting mechanics were really easy to learn but not boring.

The games graphics are good but the art style direction they chose compared to other dragon age games looks out of place and almost childish. That being said the character creation is fairly good with a lot of face customisation to play around with.

The dialog is... After the intro of the game I lost ALL interest in any dialog not dealing with solas or the main quest. It is very childish and awkward writing. What is with all the apologizing?
10 hours into a Dragon Age game and I dropped the game.

Maybe next time create a new IP for your modern audience instead of ruining a great one.

I was a bit skeptical at first given that I've been burned in the past by BioWare, but I actually genuinely love this game. It's more of an action/adventure set up than the standard RPG of past Dragon Age games. It borrows heavily from a Mass Effect style combat system, but that's actually preferable for me. I enjoy that some of the story elements that were pulled in from other Dragon Age media, and liked all of the companions and overarching plot.

Just be prepared for it to lean more in the direction of Mass Effect/Dragon Age 2 style linear maps from a base and tighter focus on your team as opposed to something more open and broader reaching like Inquisition.
FIx your shit with the dragon fights. after the first phase, the second phase doenst seem to work and im stuck without being able to kill it

Such an incredibly massive disappointment. Everything that made the previous games - even DA2, which was underwhelming - fun is gone, and a hollow husk is all that remains in their place. 

The maps are empty. There's no one to talk to, no environments to interact with, nothing to find, no space to even explore. Each environment is basically a "Go from point A to point B, and maybe we'll put a random chest with pointless trinkets in it for you to find if we're feeling nice."

The combat is button mashing and repetitive. The puzzles, if you can call them that, are "put this thing here, then that thing there, then push the button that lets your unplayable, two-dimensional companion use their special power, then climb the thing." Items are pointless, weapons and armor come in preconstructed sets and are mostly cosmetic; there's no mixing and matching and finding what's just right for your character and playstyle. 

Even the voice actors sound bored. I expect they realized they were basically just polishing a turd and decided to phone it in like everyone else obviously did. 

I don't even know if I'd enjoy the story since I can't focus on it at all; everything is is just so completely vapid that my brain wants nothing to do with it. 

This game made me so sad.

This is a great game. The beginning is a bit rough ... and some of the dialogue is a bit over the top ... but overall its a great game ... a story well told. The graphics are amazing. I particularly liked how deep the companion stories are. I don't get why this game got so many negative reviews... as a long time fan of dragon age I really enjoyed this one and wish they were following up with DLCs (I understand they are not). If you liked the previous dragon age games, you will like this one as long as you stick around past the first few hours.

For a Dragon Age game? It's underwhelming, to be totally honest.

Rook is such a flat and uninspiring character, and since they are the character you play as, it's just a bit of a slog. It feels like Rook is destined to be a sort of standard Hero archetype no matter what you do. The charm of the older Dragon Age games that allows you to play a nuanced character feels lost in this one. Very few of the decisions or dialog options feel like they really matter. The decisions you made in past games feel even less relevant. The combat is okay, but feels very button-mashy after a while. If you are a diehard Dragon Age fan, it might be worth it for the lore, but I honestly can't see myself playing it again.

Ignore refunded, bought elsewhere.

Not nearly as bad as everyone says who watched a youtube video to be told what to think about the game.

Beautiful presentation, actually good story, some decent punchy combat, a bit of theorycrafting with builds and gear, and some good voice acting.

On sale this is easily a recommend, just go into it without needing the rely on everyone else on the internet to tell you what to think about it.

The hate this game got is partially understandable. Personally, though, I enjoyed it immensely, the action/combat is very well done, the character development and romance paths well written for the most part, and it was generally a great ending for the world of Thedas. 

The difficult thing with the last game of a franchise is wrapping up on all the loose ends, filling in the blanks of past stories, and making the main character competent enough to be the last leader standing. That probably caused the devs to limit the roleplaying element to more of a neutral/good playthrough. Some options could easily be interchanged with "evil" ones, but ultimately the point of the game was to save the world of Thedas from the Blight and malevolent Gods, which would not make sense to do with an Evil character.

All in all, it is a great game and a good sequel to DA:I, while also being a bad sequel to the amazing worldbuilding of DA:O. Neve Gallus made up for it though :)

Begins slow. But every second story wise gets better and better. You do quests even with simple discussions and you connect and care for your companions at some point forward. The story was fun for me and heroic and i enjoyed it. You make choices that matter in the ending - and companions can die if you are not careful -and all story dialogues are actors with nice voice acting that keeps the story alive and feels like you live in it, i know i didnt skip it. The controls combat and gameplay was just decent-average and the difficulty was easy-mediocre for relaxing at your free hours. I would rate it at 8. The epic ending was enough for me to recommend it to anyone.

I love the Dragon Age Franchise and wish they would make more games in the series, I love that I can have romance options and that I can even settle down with whomever I choose. I enjoy every minute of my time in the world of Dragon Age.

I held off from playing this game in fear it wouldn't be on par with the previous DA games. I should have hopped on sooner lol. First off, the character creation is such a huge upgrade from DA Inquisition. It's very similar to the Baldur's Gate 3 character creation except DA Veilguard does an exceptional job by giving you sliders to customize to your hearts content. Rook looks amazing in the cutscenes and the graphics are phenomenal. I enjoy the combat system and love how fluid it feels. I added a couple of mods to heighten my experience with the game (I highly recommend going on Nexus Mods). It made my experience with the game 100x better! There are so many missions to do and and the storyline is great and immersive. Please give this game a try and don't mind the negative reviews. I didn't think I would enjoy the game but I'm 33 hours deep into it and only had the game for a week. For anyone that has played Inquisition and the previous games, there are so many cameos and references to give that bit of nostalgia :)

tbh if this wasn't a dragon age game i would've totally recommended it, veilguard was a very enjoyable game to play also a very pretty one but in the end it doesn't matter because it's a DRAGON AGE game and it just lack the dragon age essence. 
All the important topics from the previous games were abandonded, nothing we did before matters and it lacks in the terms of the heavy atmosphere. I never felt like any of my choices really mattered or like anything i said influenced my relationship with the characters at all. their banter is also very soulless and not as engaging as it used to be. not to mention how all the romances feel almost nonexistent.
It's just dull story and character wise and preforms weakly next to the older games.
i wish the developers would listen to the wishes of their fanbase because this game really had a big potential, shame.

I really enjoyed this game after fully completing it, I even did all of the sidequests which I haven't done in any of the other games before. I have played all of the dragon age games in the franchise and this one is definitly one of my favorites.
It's very different from the other games but every dragon age game has always been different from origins.
If this seems like a game for you but the bad reviews are holding you off, I really recommend you to give it a try. But play the other games before you do, it's such an amazing franchise!!

I did have some audio/lag issues but was able to resolve most of it.

Please Bioware make another game!! I will buy.

I really wanted to like this game. I loved all the previous Dragon Age titles. But this isn't really a Dragon Age game, it's a puzzle game in a Dragon Age wrapper. And I hate puzzle games. Follow your quest marker for a while to a door. It's locked! And you need to solve some stupid puzzle to open it. All of these types of games have a puzzle or two for some reason, but this one really overdoes it.

5/10 design team did pretty well, writing team did not. Follows the same format as mass effect 2, quest to get companion then quest to get companion loyalty. Im not really a fan of that format but a lot of people love it I guess. That being said the only reason I think it worked for mass effect 2 is good writing and likeable companions. The actual combat feels like a watered down version of god of war, its solid but not amazing. Companions cant be controlled and you can only activate moves once in a while. They also dont vary that much so it really doesnt matter which ones you bring really. Really just couldnt get into the story, not sure why but it just didnt really draw me in. Also it seems like there were a lot of times where they ended up going towards the "the previous lore said this, but that was actually wrong." I think they could have gotten away with one or two of those but there were like 8 times it happened. Overall, if you are looking for an RPG there are just much better ones out there.

First three games were my favourite games, especially Origins, the first. Dark fantasy, great graphics, psychological at times, dark and detailed with the derangements, but still funny with the comebacks and sassiness.
This has none of that and disregards lore, have to baby the worst character that I was most excited for. Waited 10 years. Terrible.

Great Graphics, ok gameplay, terrible character-story writing. 0 replayability as all classes generally feel the same, this is not a dragon age game at all ( you cannot take control of your companions ???). I was one of those to believe and love this game with all my heart despite the hate, bought it full price on day one of release, gave it all i could but after finishing the story it just left me with a feeling of a huge disappointment. I really hope for a decent Dragon Age game like Origins or Inquisition not this one.
It's not the worst game ever, but it's not a Dragon Age either, it's just an average RPG like many other.

tldr.text: Mixed (68%): players love the story and characters, but the same theme draws the most complaints.
Reviews from the last 30 days are much more negative than the all-time score.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about the price more often, with 18% of recent reviews raising it against 10% overall, so the cost deserves a second look before buying.
Players with under 2 hours are much less positive than players with over 50 hours, a gap that suggests early impressions are harsher than long-term views.
